transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Schiavone.
The Salvador native who was mistakenly deported back to El Salvador, Kilmar Abrego-Garcia,
is now leaving the U.S. to "a country of his choosing."
Abrego-Garcia's senator, Democrat Chris Van Holland of Maryland, has posted on social
media that he is happy that Kilmar is about to put an end to a very rough immigration
story.
Abrego-Garcia had faced the prospect of his unfinished immigration case ending with deportation
to a country where he did not choose to live.
Van Holland says Kilmar is a "free man."
President Trump is leading the cheering for Jensen Wong's return as CEO of NVIDIA, but
not everyone is pleased, and Pierre's Andrea Shue reports.
Unfathomable. A backslide. Those are words that some are using to describe the decision
by NVIDIA's board to reinstate Wong after finding him in violation of the company's
code of conduct.
Frieda Kaper Klein has long used her role as an investor to promote diversity and inclusion
in Silicon Valley. She says Wong's swift comeback sends a troubling message.
You can violate corporate policy. You can possibly threaten national security. You can
make up your own rules as you go, as long as you bring in the money.
Videos posted to social media show Wong arriving at company headquarters to loud applause.
He tells the crowd he'll be a better CEO the second time around. Andrea Shue, NPR News.
President Trump has awarded Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom, and Pierre's
Franco Ordonez reports the former New York City mayor and Trump ally received the country's
highest civilian honor in a private White House ceremony.
President Trump has repeatedly referred to Rudy Giuliani as the greatest mayor in the
history of New York City. The White House hailed his "lasting impact" on both New York
City and the nation. Giuliani is famous for his role leading New York in the aftermath
of the September 11, 2001 attacks. He ran unsuccessfully for president in 2008, but
then had quite a fall in the public eye. Giuliani, who served as Trump's personal lawyer during
his efforts to overturn the 2020 election, was later sanctioned by the courts and was
disbarred in both New York and Washington for making false statements about the election.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News, The White House.
The Army says it's taking numerous precautions as it prepares to detonate five tons of degraded
and dangerous lead azide in southeastern Iowa. The stockpile will be detonated tomorrow to
prevent a spontaneous, uncontrolled explosion. On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average
gained 423 points today, closing at 50,018. The Nasdaq retreated 356. This is NPR News
in Washington.
In the San Francisco Bay area, people are on alert for heavy rain and high King tides
that could cause flooding in low-lying coastal communities. Over this Thanksgiving week,
the Pacific Northwest and parts of South Florida are also watching tide levels.
A joint European-Japanese mission has successfully launched into orbit around the planet Mercury.
But as Joe Palka reports, things didn't go exactly as planned.
The mission is called "Beppi Colombo." It's actually made up of two probes, a Japanese-built
orbiter for studying Mercury's magnetic field, and a European orbiter for studying the planet's
surface features and chemistry. On Saturday, November 21, when Beppi Colombo was just 400
miles from the planet, the main engine fired right on time, but later analysis showed the
engine cut off unexpectedly, putting the spacecraft into an orbit further from the planet than
it intended. Mission managers are still determining exactly why this happened, but they say they
can still achieve all of the mission's planned scientific objectives.
For NPR News, I'm Joe Palka.
Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies has been convicted by a U.S. jury in New York
of bank fraud and conspiracy to steal trade secrets. In a case that was launched seven
years ago, federal prosecutors argued Huawei had a pattern of stealing technological secrets
from competitors and partners in the U.S. and elsewhere and did business in countries
subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran and North Korea. Huawei has not been allowed
to sell equipment to United States carriers for years. I'm Louise Kivoni, NPR News, Washington.
